hero.description: Terra is a simple open source dashboard for monitoring terrarium measurements, visualizing trends, and keeping a readable history.

project.title: The project
project.subtitle: A small tool for monitoring a connected terrarium without unnecessary layers.

need.title: A real need
need.description: When measurements pile up, it quickly becomes hard to see what is actually changing. The goal is to make the terrarium state easier to read.

why.title: Why it exists
why.description: Less time reading raw data means more time observing, adjusting the environment, and doing the right maintenance.

today.title: Today
today.description: The project already handles data ingestion, charts, recent history, and a few useful tools around monitoring.

technical.title: The technical side, kept simple
technical.description: A modern web architecture focused on reliability, speed, and clarity.
paragraphs: The application centralizes measurements sent by sensors so they can be reviewed quickly in a clear interface.
Data is automatically aggregated to surface useful trends while keeping the UI readable on both mobile and desktop.
Behind the scenes, the project relies on modern web technologies chosen to deliver a robust experience that stays easy to evolve.

team.title: Who is building it
paragraphs: I launched Terra to solve a very concrete need: having reliable and understandable monitoring for a connected terrarium. I build the project end to end, from data ingestion to the interface.
The goal stays simple: a useful, readable tool that remains open enough to improve over time.

follow.title: Where to find the project
follow.description: The GitHub repository is the best place to inspect the code, follow the project, or suggest improvements.
